0: In practice a general image-generation model cannot always generate a specified person, product or visual style accurately. If you want the model to produce a particular character, product or style, you can train a LoRA. This chapter first introduces the basic concepts of image-generation models and LoRA, then completes an image LoRA training run with DiffSynth.
2: The common image-generation models today consist mainly of a text encoder, a diffusion model and a VAE. After the user enters a prompt, the model understands the text, gradually generates image features, and finally converts those features into an image you can view.
3: The text encoder understands the prompt, turning the words into text features the model can process. For example, given “an orange cat wearing sunglasses sitting on a beach”, the text encoder encodes “orange cat”, “sunglasses”, “beach” and so on as conditions for later image generation.
4: The diffusion model is the core component. Starting from random noise, it removes noise step by step over several passes according to the text features, forming the objects, colours and structure in the image. For example, when generating the image above, the first frame is just random noise, and after several rounds the orange cat, the sunglasses and the beach take shape.
5: The VAE (Variational Autoencoder) converts between image space and feature space. To reduce computation, a diffusion model usually does not work directly at high resolution but generates in a compressed feature space. Once generation is done, the VAE turns the image features back into the final image.

7: After the user enters a prompt, the model goes through text encoding, image-feature generation and image restoration in turn and finally produces the image. Different image-generation models differ in their exact structure, but all complete the transformation from text input to image output.
9: General image-generation models are usually trained on a large number of images and can generate many kinds of content, but for a particular person, product or visual style the result may not be accurate enough.
10: For example, when you want the model to generate a specific product, even a detailed description of its colour, shape and appearance may produce a result quite different from the real product.
11: You can train the model to learn these new visual features, but retraining the whole model needs a lot of training data and compute. For learning a specific feature like this you can use the parameter-efficient method LoRA, whose principle is described in section 9.2 of this book. Training freezes most of the original model's parameters and trains only a small number of new ones, so the model learns the new feature.
12: Training an image LoRA needs only a few target images to let the model learn a particular person, product, style or other visual feature. The resulting LoRA file is much smaller than the full model. To use it you load the original model and then the corresponding LoRA, and the newly learned visual feature becomes available.
14: Depending on the learning goal, image LoRA can be divided into style LoRA, character LoRA, product LoRA and concept LoRA.
16: A style LoRA learns the overall visual style of an image: colour, line, composition, expression. Training needs a set of images in a similar painting style; the content may differ, but the overall style should stay as consistent as possible.
17: For example: training a style LoRA on a set of ink-wash paintings lets the model generate people, animals or landscapes in an ink-wash style.
19: Test prompt: a panda sitting in a bamboo grove eating bamboo.
22: As you can see, loading the style LoRA turns the image into an ink-wash painting.
24: A character LoRA mainly learns the appearance of a specific person: face, hairstyle and overall look. Training needs images of the same person from different angles, expressions, backgrounds and clothing, so the model learns their relatively stable appearance. Once trained, prompts can put this person in different states in an office, on a street or on a snowy mountain.
25: Example: provide several casual photos of a young man and let the model learn his appearance.
26: Test prompt: a young man sitting in the subway looking at his phone.
28: With the character LoRA loaded, the model keeps the face, hairstyle and other appearance features stable.
30: A product LoRA mainly learns the appearance of a specific product: packaging, shape, colour and signature structure. Training can use images of the same product from different angles, backgrounds and lighting, so the model learns its relatively fixed appearance. Once trained, the product can be placed in different display scenarios to generate product showcases, e-commerce assets and advertising images.
31: Example: prepare a set of images of sports shoes to advertise, let the model learn the product's features and generate an ad image.
32: Test prompt: a pair of white sports shoes on concrete pavement on a modern city street. Morning sunlight from the side, blurred modern buildings and city road in the background, sports-brand advertising photography style, low camera angle, shallow depth of field.
34: With the product LoRA loaded, the result keeps the sports shoes' appearance features.
36: A concept LoRA learns an abstract visual concept or combination of features, such as a futuristic city, mechanical architecture, sci-fi elements or a particular costume element. Unlike a character or product LoRA, a concept LoRA does not learn one specific object but visual features shared by several objects. Training needs a set of images sharing a similar concept; the concrete content may differ, but the overall conceptual features should stay consistent.
37: Example: prepare a set of futuristic tech-city images and let the model learn futuristic architecture, smart devices and sci-fi visual elements.
38: Test prompt: a futuristic tech city, grand floating buildings and aerial traffic, flying cars weaving through the air, huge ring tracks and holographic ads, blue sky and white clouds, cinematic composition, a thoroughly futuristic sci-fi atmosphere.
40: With the concept LoRA loaded, the result shows the visual elements of a futuristic tech city.
42: DiffSynth is an open-source framework for image and video generation, editing and training.
43: Training an image LoRA involves loading the base model, reading the training data, configuring training parameters, running the LoRA training and saving the model. DiffSynth wraps these steps and provides a training script for each image-generation model. You only need to prepare the training data as the model requires and configure the parameters to start LoRA training.
44: DiffSynth also provides image-generation pipelines. Once training is done you can load the base model and the trained LoRA weights directly and generate images from prompts to test whether the LoRA learned the target feature. Training and testing can be done in the same framework.
